pr_title: Reduce follower cluster state lag timeout for disruption tests
pr_body:
It's possible for a node-left task to get interrupted prior to removing
the node from the master's list of faultyNodes. Nodes on the faultyNodes
list do not receive cluster state updates, and are eventually removed.

Subsequently, when the node attempts to rejoin, after test network
disruptions have ceased, the node-join request can succeed, but the
node will never receive the cluster state update, consider the node-join
a failure, and will resend node-join requests until the LagDetector
removes the node from the faultyNodes list.
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/108690 will address the
node-join issue.

Closes #91447

------------------------------------
Much belatedly circling back to this.

comments: This used to reproduce (almost) reliably with `-Dtests.seed=F227DC2661BD3347`. However, this doesn't seem to be the case anymore. I suspect these failures were due to the desired-balance allocator changes, and it seems to have been resolved, as @DaveCTurner and @idegtiarenko were addressing other failures. I would still look into this out of interest as this seems to be a special test suite with a complicated history! If I do not see anything special, I'll just close this since I might be chasing a potentially resolved issue.

Hmm I don't think we've fixed anything that might have prevented the cluster from stabilising in a reasonable timeframe, which appears to be the problem here. But maybe we have.

That seems suspicious, and unrelated to allocator changes.

So the [Coordinator will publish the new cluster state](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2f956608f16d5648c7c95582417a453dffdf88f7/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/coordination/Coordinator.java#L1582-L1584), and it calls into the [FollowersChecker to remove faulty nodes if they are no longer part of the cluster state](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2f956608f16d5648c7c95582417a453dffdf88f7/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/coordination/FollowersChecker.java#L147-L151). The only other paths that I see to clear faulty nodes is when the node [becomes a follower](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2f956608f16d5648c7c95582417a453dffdf88f7/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/coordination/Coordinator.java#L968) or [becomes a candidate](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2f956608f16d5648c7c95582417a453dffdf88f7/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/coordination/Coordinator.java#L854).

In this test failure scenario, a faulty node (node_t1) joins a cluster with master node_t2. So the cluster state being published [should contain node_t1, which I think will leave node_t1 marked as a faulty node](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2f956608f16d5648c7c95582417a453dffdf88f7/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/coordination/FollowersChecker.java#L149). I haven't been able to reproduce the failure. Next I'll see if I can write a new test in FollwersCheckerTests to cover the scenario, and see what happens.

A node is marked as faulty in the FollowersChecker [when there is a network disconnection with the that node](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/083b59122b3cdf5168d2d2351e53fca99009baf5/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/coordination/FollowersChecker.java#L136-L141). A node is not returned to not-faulty unless a master election occurs or the node is removed from the cluster, as mentioned above. I think the failed run differs in marking a node as faulty but never removes it -- which would [remove the node from the faultyNodes list](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2f956608f16d5648c7c95582417a453dffdf88f7/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/coordination/FollowersChecker.java#L149-L151)

So the question becomes: why didn't the node get removed properly from the cluster state?

The logic to remove the node -- node-left cluster state update -- is [scheduled right after logging "marking node as faulty"](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/083b59122b3cdf5168d2d2351e53fca99009baf5/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/coordination/FollowersChecker.java#L386-L390). That [leads](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2f956608f16d5648c7c95582417a453dffdf88f7/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/coordination/Coordinator.java#L290) back to the Coordinator, [removeNode](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/2f956608f16d5648c7c95582417a453dffdf88f7/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/coordination/Coordinator.java#L359-L366).

The removeNode code actually was significantly changed [9 months ago](url), to [improve the master service batch queuing system](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/92021). Maybe something was wrong with the batching, such that the cluster state wasn't updated properly. But this might be enough investigation to put the failure to rest because the code has changed greatly.

UPDATE:
This NullPointerException [was fixed](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/commit/4a392e295227ee7c2e7bbd33a54450f2addfc268#diff-3b0ab75398e06bcff863305ac1b6e725917476eb32d5c2ccbf09e1ed884405f7R422-R424) a week after this test failure first occurred, Nov 18th.

> I was thinking that a successful node join should also go into FollowersChecker to remove itself from potentially being on the faultyNodes list.

That might work, but I think I'd rather refuse to let a faulty node join the cluster in the first place, retrying its removal as necessary. The trouble is that "successful node join" is not very well-defined, the master might think a join was successful even if the joining node does not, and this could lead to a situation where the node keeps on joining without fault detection properly removing it first.

> I found this NullPointerException 😁

Ahh that'd do it I reckon. I tried to reproduce the race I guessed at in [my previous comment](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/91447#issuecomment-1831736366) by adding a delay that should provoke it, but have not succeeded after several hundred attempts. But this NPE would cause the same problem without needing a re-election.

Chatted more with David about this, to get a better understanding of how cluster state updates work.

The general outline of the proposed fix would be to
- add node-left logic to the [validateJoinRequest](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/143f4208d1bb6942a5be7054d074be970390523e/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/coordination/Coordinator.java#L672-L713) func if the joining node is found to have been partially removed, in the sense of this failure where the node is still part of the cluster state but also in the [faultyNodes](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/143f4208d1bb6942a5be7054d074be970390523e/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/coordination/FollowersChecker.java#L102) list. The validation function already makes network calls, so waiting for cluster state to publish is fine.
- and then [processJoinRequest](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/143f4208d1bb6942a5be7054d074be970390523e/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/coordination/Coordinator.java#L755-L781) will proceed as usual to run the node-join logic.

Quick fix, but testing might be hard, if we want to test this failure case. Perhaps something contrived could be tested, where we reach into components and make artificial alterations, and then check that it gets sorted out.
Filed https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/108690 for the production fix, and published a PR for the test fix https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/108691
